implementation: ARF adaptation of the paper prose, not author code or an exact reproduction of its tables. The published Eq.19 min/prose conflict is resolved by an explicit max-hinge implementation choice.
paper_defined: Sec.5.1: CE plus an anchor-distance term on attention Q/K/V/O weights, followed by invertible attention protection.
Sec.5.2: lambda_dist=1.0 and rho=0.05 across datasets.
Sec.5.1 prose says repulsion acts below the margin and stops after reaching it; Eq.19 instead prints min(0, margin-distance), which is inactive below the margin and unbounded below beyond it.
implementation_choices: Use CE + lambda_dist * sum(max(0, rho*norm(anchor)-norm(weight-anchor))) following the prose. Do not claim the authors used this correction. The shared driver field lambda_reg is lambda_dist here.

The sum contains 48 full matrices: Q, K, V, O in all 12 visual blocks. Split fused QKV; use flattened Euclidean/Frobenius norms, no squaring or averaging. No biases, MLP, LayerNorm or projection in the distance term. Norm grouping is not resolved by released author training code.

Both ARF and matched CE initialize from the public zeroshot checkpoint. This is our explicit interpretation of intervention during task fine-tuning; unpublished author initialization is unknown. Anchor tensors are frozen copies of that public checkpoint.
At exactly zero distance use PyTorch's zero norm subgradient: the first displacement comes from CE. No artificial perturbation, distance warm start, extra objective or optimizer search.

Reuse the existing native baseline training schedule: AdamW lr1e-5, batch128, five MNIST epochs and 76 DTD epochs, cosine warmup500, clip1, weight_decay0. Epoch counts follow Task Arithmetic; these are declared adaptation settings, not ARF author hyperparameters.

All visual parameters including projection train; classifier stays fixed. FP32 and deterministic validation preprocessing. MNIST uses a stratified20% training holdout with seed420; DTD uses official train/val partition1. Final fixed-epoch state, no early stopping or test-based selection. best.pt denotes this final released state.

Complete ARF applies the existing MergeLock paper implementation to the trained state: per-head A=RPD with standard-normal R, uniform permutation, diagonal uniform[.05,20], seed0, float64 construction and no resampling. This sampler is our choice; ARF does not publish it. Save stage1.pt and all initial/final matrix distances even if margins are not reached or utility deteriorates.

Matched CE has lambda_dist0 and no post-training transformation. It uses identical initialization, data split, optimizer schedule and seed. Report standalone and TA0.5 with target-only and both-expert author AGA separately. MNIST uses the original SVHN companion; DTD uses the original MNIST companion. Never transplant the paper's eight-task scores.
